core_obligations: Set up (proof lines 1667-1674): let m be a maximal ideal and A -> B an etale map with a prime q over m; by the description of the strict henselization it suffices to show that A_m = B_q.

Separate the primes over m (proof lines 1674-1682): there are finitely many primes q = q_1, ..., q_n over m and no specializations among them because an etale map is quasi-finite; choosing g in the intersection of the other q_i and outside q and replacing B by B_g leaves q as the only prime over m.

Produce a faithfully flat etale map with a retraction (proof lines 1682-1690): the image U of Spec(B) -> Spec(A) is open, so there is f not in m with Spec(A) = U union D(f); the map A -> B x A_f is faithfully flat and etale, hence has a retraction sigma by hypothesis.

Conclude that the local map is an isomorphism (proof lines 1690-1699): sigma is flat as a map between etale A-algebras; since q is the only prime of B x A_f over m, one obtains a flat retraction of A_p -> B_q, and since flat local homomorphisms are injective the composite of two flat local maps equal to the identity forces both to be isomorphisms, so A_m = B_q as required.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an isomorphism of the local rings using the description of the strict henselization.
Arrange that a single prime lies over the maximal ideal by inverting an element.
Adjoin a localization to make the etale map faithfully flat and use the hypothesis to get a retraction.
Conclude with flatness and injectivity of flat local maps.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that if every faithfully flat etale ring map A -> B has a retraction, then every local ring of A at a maximal ideal is strictly henselian (statement lines 1660-1665). The proof (proof lines 1667-1700) isolates a single prime over the maximal ideal by inverting an element, builds a faithfully flat etale map whose image covers the spectrum together with a localization, applies the hypothesis to get a retraction, and concludes by flatness and injectivity of flat local homomorphisms. H2: a three-step reduction with four inputs, written out in full.
